summary: A 1966 steel tower on Barden Hill, replacing a mid-1910s predecessor; the town's very first lookout was a room in Middleboro's Town Hall observatory.

facts.agency: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Control

events.note: NHLR gives 1913 for the first Barden Hill tower (48 ft), replacing an earlier lookout post in the Middleboro Town Hall observatory room. A Boston Daily Globe article from March 1915 describes the Barden Hill steel tower as still being planned at that date, conflicting with NHLR's 1913 date.
Current 75 ft steel tower with 10x10 ft cab built, replacing the earlier Barden Hill tower.
Registered December 15, 2004, nominated by Henry Isenberg.

corrections.proposed: Consider noting this is the second tower on the site: an earlier ~48 ft steel tower stood on Barden Hill from the mid-1910s (NHLR says 1913; a contemporary newspaper account suggests 1915-16) before being replaced in 1966.
corrections.evidence: NHLR detail page description field, plus a March 1915 Boston Daily Globe item reproduced on easternuslookouts.weebly.com/barden-hill.html describing the tower as still planned, and a 1918 State Forester report noting a recently-installed staircase.

notes_for_editor: NHLR and the 1915 Boston Daily Globe item disagree on when the first Barden Hill tower went up (1913 vs. apparently still 'planned' in March 1915); kept both in the story rather than picking one. No source found addresses current staffing, access, or climbability, so those stay unknown in the tower record. The easternuslookouts.weebly.com page carries a banner image but it isn't clearly captioned as depicting this specific tower, so it was not added to photos.
